body: Cases: Monster (outsourced bottling + distributors; best US stock of 30 years, ~+200,000%), Costco (membership fees ~ most of profit; ~29x since 2009), Constellation Software (~300x via small VMS acquisitions funded by FCF), Domino's (franchise; ~180x from trough), Hermès (scarcity pricing; ~30x), Booking (agency model). Shared traits: high returns on incremental capital, someone else funds the assets (co-packers, franchisees, suppliers via negative working capital, customers via membership fees), long-tenured owner-managers (Sacks/Schlosberg, Munger's influence, Leonard, Dumas family), and EPS growth doing most of the work for a decade or more. Early signals: rising gross margin with flat capex, renewal/retention data, management letters reporting ROIC honestly. Where they stall: (1) key-person exit plus a new threat (Constellation -51% after Leonard left + AI fears); (2) the multiple gets ahead of growth (Costco ~50-60x on high-single-digit growth; Hermès ~50x before a ~-50% fall); (3) growth slows to GDP-plus (Monster 2022-24, Domino's 2022-26). Lesson: these are the best 'hold forever' candidates, but late-stage returns depend on entry multiple; a P/E doubling in the last stretch is a non-repeatable gift.
